sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Durgan was an Irish heroine. She was an unfortunate Irishwoman. Her own truthtelling destroyed her. Herccad was her mother. Herccad slept with one of her slaves. This act was a disgrace. Durgan reported the affair to her father. Herccad then arranged to have her daughter killed. The murder hid the shame. Durgan's honest words cost her own life.
objective: Record Durgan as an Irish heroine whose truthtelling led to her own death.
